Permanent test inputs

Source: vignettes/articles/contributor-tests-testthat-fixtures-readme.Rmd
contributor-tests-testthat-fixtures-readme.Rmd

Contributing · Object model · Discovery walkthrough · Object fields

These files are inputs to tests of current SCEPTRE behavior. They contain no historical p-value, effect-estimate or random-stream output snapshots. provenance.json records their SHA256 values; update it deliberately when an input changes, alongside the reason and affected tests.

  • refactor/inputs.rds, cases.rds and backed-inputs.rds describe synthetic counts, covariates and seven workflow configurations. The counts include a strong positive effect, a zero-count gene, failed-QC pairs, nonconsecutive retained cells and overlapping high-MOI guide assignments.
  • refactor/native-inputs.rds contains explicitly constructed score arrays and draw lists, plus sampler settings. Stage labels describe the intended examples; tests also check independent effect/SE formulas and selected draw segments. Sampler settings cover the three production samplers. The helper supplies current function names; retired samplers and unused historical name fields remain only in the temporary comparison suite.
  • aggregation-inputs-6a43fa5.rds is a frozen set of 28 count-matrix/metadata examples introduced at 6a43fa5: duplicate triplets and metadata, stored zeros, logical/pattern matrices and rounding-sensitive counts. Keep these inputs frozen; add new examples in the test when extending coverage. Expectations are calculated from dense algebra during the current test, not saved outputs.
  • saved-objects/sceptre-0.99.0-21f9ea0.rds is an in-memory object written by source-verified SCEPTRE 0.99.0 at 21f9ea098b69c444a884a49bc254de711968e3b5. It is the prepared low-MOI/complement/permutation toy analysis, before discovery. Its original bytes were preserved from the refactor characterization fixture. The current package must read it and resume equivalently to a newly prepared object. Do not regenerate it with current SCEPTRE: it is a versioned file-format example, much like a test input written by an older file-format implementation. No old executable or old expected result is required by this test.

To recreate the four mathematical/workflow input files in a fresh directory:

Rscript --vanilla tools/fixtures/generate-inputs.R /absolute/fresh/input-directory

This uses current test-input recipes, R, Matrix and withr, without loading SCEPTRE or its original implementation. Compare the R objects with identical(readRDS(a), readRDS(b)); compressed bytes can differ across R versions. Review input changes rather than automatically replacing fixtures during CI. The bridge C++ file is small test-only code for constructing and inspecting draw banks.
